key_insight: Epitaxial 0.5PZT-0.5PFN thin films show a strong, reversible photocurrent response that depends on ferroelectric polarization, indicating coupled ferroelectric–photovoltaic behavior in a single-phase multiferroic.
engineering_relevance: These films are promising for next-generation optoelectronic devices, especially polarization-tunable photovoltaics and nonvolatile memory elements.
method: Grew highly oriented 0.5Pb(Zr0.52Ti0.48)O3–0.5Pb(Fe0.5Nb0.5)O3 thin films by pulsed laser deposition.
Used SrTiO3(001) substrates with a SrRuO3 bottom electrode.
Characterized structure, ferroelectricity, magnetism, and photoresponse under 403 nm laser illumination.
evidence_signal: The films were single-phase and (001)-oriented, with remanent polarization around 17 μC/cm², weak ferromagnetism at room temperature, and polarization-dependent photocurrent reaching ±20 μA/cm².
watch_item: Performance is demonstrated on epitaxial thin films under monochromatic laser illumination, so device-level scalability, spectral response, and long-term stability still need validation.
paper_title: Enhanced Photocurrent Response in Epitaxial 0.5PZT-0.5PFN Multiferroic Thin Films
